name: Indian Oil Corporation Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest integrated oil company (Maharatna PSU, government ~71% incl. 19.6% other govt holders): ~80 MMTPA refining across 10 refineries (~33% of India's capacity), ~50% share of petroleum product sales through ~40,000 fuel stations, 14,500+ km of product/crude pipelines, LPG and petrochemicals (~4 MMT), plus gas, lubricants, renewables and EV ventures. Retail petrol/diesel/LPG prices are quasi-administered, so marketing margins swing opposite to crude while refining margins swing with it. Q2 FY27 PAT Rs 21.6k cr (record, with inventory gains) after a Q1 loss.

revenue_mix.segment: petroleum products - domestic marketing (petrol, diesel, LPG, ATF)

exposures.mechanism: Brent +10% (~$9.5/bbl). Retail petrol/diesel/LPG prices are frozen, so marketing under-recovers ~Rs5.6/litre while GRM and inventory gains offset. Calibration from the quarter-to-quarter swing: IOC operating profit fell from Rs 24.8k cr (Mar-26) to Rs 4.1k cr (Jun-26) when Brent spiked, then rebounded to Rs 33.8k cr in Sep-26 with inventory gains. A sustained +10% costs roughly Rs 10k cr/yr after GRM uplift (~ -17% of normalised EBITDA ~Rs 60k cr) x EV/MCap 1.7 x persistence 0.25 (govt compensation / price hikes) => ~-7 gross; the market evidently discounts compensation and pass-through (pack elasticity -1.80, t -3.7), so shrink toward data: -2.2.

evidence.note: ICRA: OMCs lose Rs530 cr/day at retail prices frozen; OMCs seek Rs75,000 cr, Centre to decide in 2027 (Moneycontrol 7 Sep)
Q2 FY27 PAT Rs21,630 cr (standalone) on refining margins + inventory gains (The Hindu, CNBC TV18, Investing.com)

exposures.mechanism: GRM +$2/bbl on ~75 MMT throughput (~550m bbl): +$1.1bn = ~Rs 10k cr pre-tax (~17% of normalised EBITDA Rs 60k cr) x EV/MCap 1.7 x persistence 0.3 (margin spikes fade within 2-3 quarters) = +8.7 theoretical; haircut 50% for tax, windfall-levy leakage and for the pack's contrary estimate => +4.0. Pack shows -1.30 (t -2.8) because the series (HO=F, heating-oil futures) co-moves with Brent, so the pack coefficient mostly reflects crude-level exposure already in the Brent edge; sign conflict explained, not accepted.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 PAT Rs21,630 cr (standalone) on refining margins + inventory gains (The Hindu, CNBC TV18, Investing.com)

exposures.mechanism: +1 = Rs2/litre excise rise. If retail prices are held, OMCs absorb it: ~78bn litres petrol+diesel x Rs2 = Rs15.6k cr (26% of normalised EBITDA). Government usually times excise changes against crude declines (neutral for OMCs) and the 1 Nov 2026 'tax twist' headline concerns this; assume 25% absorbed x 26% x 1.7 x 0.15 persistence => ~-1.0.

evidence.note: ICRA: OMCs lose Rs530 cr/day at retail prices frozen; OMCs seek Rs75,000 cr, Centre to decide in 2027 (Moneycontrol 7 Sep)

exposures.mechanism: IOC exports only ~5-8% of throughput (model knowledge), so export levies on diesel/petrol/ATF cut realisations on a small volume: Rs 6/L on ~3 MMT exports ~ Rs 2.2k cr = 3.7% of normalised EBITDA x 1.7 x persistence 0.15 => -0.9.

evidence.note: Export levies on petrol/diesel/ATF reset repeatedly Aug-Oct 2026

exposures.mechanism: INR 3% weaker raises crude import cost (all USD) before retail resets; USD borrowings (~$6bn, model knowledge) create MTM losses; product price parity gives only partial offset. Cost +3% on ~Rs 7 lakh cr crude bill = Rs 21k cr gross, ~85% recovered via import-parity pricing on the refining side but not on frozen retail => net ~-Rs 3k cr = -5% EBITDA x 1.7 x 0.25 persistence => -2.1; pack -1.74 (t -1.2) agrees.
Gross debt ~Rs 1.3 lakh cr, ~40% floating: 25bp = Rs 130 cr = 0.4% of PBT; main channel is the discount rate on a 5.7%-yield, P/B 0.9 PSU. Duration approx 1.5% per 25bp x 0.4 => -0.6.

GDP +1pp lifts fuel demand ~0.8pp (diesel is GDP-elastic): IOC sells ~100 MMT, marketing margin Rs ~3.5/L on incremental volume plus refinery utilisation => EBITDA +1.5% x 1.7 x 1.0 structural, minus fuel-subsidy drag => +1.2.

Escalation (+1) ~ Brent +12% and diesel cracks wider. IOC sources ~55-60% of crude from Middle East (model knowledge) and trimmed West-Asia term volumes (Business Standard 21 Oct 2026). Marketing under-recoveries dominate (-2.6 via Brent) plus supply-security premium and freight/insurance; GRM windfall adds back +1. Net ~ -3.5. De-escalation hopes after the US midterms (4 Nov) helped OMCs rally up to 7% on 5 Nov.

evidence.note: ICRA: OMCs lose Rs530 cr/day at retail prices frozen; OMCs seek Rs75,000 cr, Centre to decide in 2027 (Moneycontrol 7 Sep)

exposures.mechanism: +1 = larger Russian discounts / freer access. IOC buys Russian Urals on spot (~25% of slate in peak years, model knowledge). $2.5/bbl discount on ~140m bbl = $350m = Rs 3.3k cr = 5.5% of normalised EBITDA x 1.7 x 0.3 => +2.8. Downside risk from the US 100% tariff threat on Russian-oil buyers (Sep 2026).

evidence.note: US 100% tariff threat on Russian-oil buyers; MEA response

exposures.mechanism: IOC petchem ~3.5 Mt polymers/PX/PTA (model knowledge): +10% spreads ~ +$60/t x 3.5 Mt = $210m = Rs 2.0k cr = 3.3% of normalised EBITDA x 1.7 x 0.35 persistence => +2.0, haircut for China oversupply => +1.5.
Gas/LNG +15%: refineries burn gas and use it for hydrogen, plus IOC Gas marketing; ~2-3% of opex => +0.4% opex x ... ~-1.5% EBITDA x 1.7 x 0.3 => -0.8. Pack -0.80 (t -2.1) agrees.

+1 = government compensation of ~Rs 25k cr to OMCs for LPG/fuel under-recoveries (OMCs seek Rs 75k cr; Centre to decide in 2027). IOC share ~38% = Rs 9.5k cr pre-tax, ~Rs 7.1k cr post-tax = 3.5% of Rs 2.05 lakh cr market cap; probability of cash (vs bonds/none) discount 0.9 => +3.2.
